tool.name: nuclei_template_update
tool.description:
Refresh the local Nuclei template database. Pulls the latest CVE detection templates from `projectdiscovery/nuclei-templates` so coverage doesn't degrade between sandbox image rebuilds. Templates ship daily; image-baked snapshots go stale within weeks.
Mechanism: shells out to `nuclei -ut -silent` (modern shortcut) or `nuclei -update-templates -silent` (legacy fallback). The Nuclei CLI handles git-pull / cache-management / template-checksum verification internally; we capture stdout + stderr, parse the version markers, and return a structured summary. Subprocess invoked with `shell=False` and a list-form argv (no shell interpretation).
Process discipline: - `nuclei` binary located via `shutil.which` (or `STRIX_NUCLEI_BIN` env override). Returns `success=False` with a clear error when the binary isn't installed. - Hard timeout (default 120s). - Output captured in memory, capped at 64 KiB (truncated suffix marked).
Throttling: - Per-process throttle: refuses to run more than once every 30 minutes against the local Nuclei templates directory (cached state under `~/.strix/nuclei_template_meta.json`). Pass `force=True` to override. - Avoids redundant updates within a multi-target scan while keeping the data fresh enough to matter.
Findings: emits a single info-severity finding (CWE-200, info_disclosure) with the update status. Useful for the run report / coverage assertions ("templates were refreshed at scan start; coverage is current as of ``") rather than for triage.
MITRE technique: T1588.006 (Obtain Capabilities: Vulnerabilities) — keeping the local CVE-detection database fresh.
Composes with cluster-A safety: `--exclude-path` doesn't apply (Nuclei talks to GitHub / projectdiscovery, not the customer's domain).

parameter.name: timeout
parameter.description: Hard timeout for the nuclei subprocess in seconds. Default 120 (templates can be ~50MB and upstream may rate-limit slow connections).

parameter.name: force
parameter.description: When True, bypasses the throttle window and always invokes nuclei. Default False (re-runs within the throttle window are skipped to avoid redundant updates within a multi-target scan).

parameter.name: throttle_seconds
parameter.description: Skip-update window in seconds. Default 1800 (30 minutes). Within this window, re-invocations are no-ops unless `force=True`.

returns.description:
{success, ran, throttled, updated, binary_path, args_used, version_before, version_after, template_count_after, duration_seconds, stdout, stderr, returncode, findings_emitted, error?}.
The agent should: 1. Invoke once at scan start (before deeper recon / vulnerability scanning) so the run uses up-to-date templates. 2. Note the `version_after` field for inclusion in the run summary / coverage assertions. 3. Treat `success=False` with `error` mentioning "nuclei binary not found" as a sandbox-image issue, not a target issue — the agent should document that CVE-detection coverage is reduced for this run.
